monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, a steady rhythm that makes The Leaking Stack feel heavy and real again. I rest my weight on the turnip, trusting the lean to hold the slip while the air above me feels thin as a breath. The turnip slides slightly, a tired thing that refuses to stay still, so I press down softer this time, hoping the lean doesn't give way under the empty weight above. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I want to press the turnip down just enough to make the lean forget it is slipping, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move or stay put while the card hums warm.

action.why: The turnip is tired and the air feels thin, so I press down again to make the lean hold.
